title: ASSEMBLY OF PISTON AND CONNECTING ROD ASSEMBLY

content.description: Piston and connecting rod assembly showing front marks on piston and connecting rod

content.text: ASSEMBLY OF PISTON AND CONNECTING ROD ASSEMBLY

items: (a) Install a new snap ring on one side of the piston pin hole.
(b) Heat the piston in hot water to approx. 60°C (140°F).
(c) Align the notch on the piston with the mark on the rod and push the piston pin in with your thumb.
(d) Install a new snap ring on the other side of the pin.
(a) Using a ring expander, install the top two compression rings with the code marks facing up.
(b) Position the piston ring end gaps so that the end gaps are in the shaded area as shown.

content.text: Do not align the end gaps.

content.description: Diagram showing piston ring positioning with upper side rail, compression ring No. 2, compression ring No. 1 & expander, lower side rail, and front mark indicated. Shaded areas show proper gap positioning.
Illustration showing hands installing bearings into connecting rod

items: (a) Install the bearings in the connecting rods and rod caps.
(b) Lubricate the face of the bearings with engine oil.
(b) Using a runout gauge, measure the circle runout at the center journal.

content.description: Crankshaft mounted on V-blocks with runout gauge measuring center journal

content.text: If the runout is greater than maximum, replace the crankshaft.

items: (c) Using a micrometer, check the diameter of the main and crank pin journal.

content.text: Measure the journals for out-of-round and taper as shown.

content.description: Cross-section diagram showing measurement points on crankshaft journal

content.text: If journals are worn, regrind or replace the crankshaft.
